Far-field is the default: it uses the mic meant for filming, on the back of the phone, which is the one facing the room when the phone lies face down on a table. Voice recognition uses the mic at the bottom edge, tuned for a phone held to your face — good in the hand, muffled on a table. USB and wired mics appear under Input device when connected.

Recap records, transcribes and summarises meetings on your phone. This policy explains what the app stores, what can leave your phone and when, and how to delete it.

IN SHORT
• No account, no ads, and no analytics or tracking of Recap's own. The developer runs no servers and receives nothing from the app.
• Your meetings stay on your phone unless you send them somewhere: by sharing or exporting, by switching to Android's speech service, or by connecting an AI endpoint.
• Two things use the network without your meeting content: model downloads you ask for, and diagnostics that Google's ML Kit (which reads text in photos) sends to Google.

WHAT IS STORED ON YOUR PHONE
All of this is kept in Recap's private storage, which other apps cannot read:
• Meetings: title, date, transcript with timings and speaker names, the language it was spoken in (when known), where an unfinished transcription stopped, your notes, summaries (one for each summary style you use), action items and reminders, highlights, topics, tags and attendee names.
• Meetings you delete, kept in Recently deleted with their audio, photos and files for 30 days (longer if the phone's clock was once set ahead) unless you erase them sooner (see DELETING YOUR DATA).
• Meeting audio, when kept. On-device transcription keeps it by default.
• Files you import: a recording, the sound of a video (only the sound is kept when it can be taken out on the phone; otherwise the whole file), or a WebVTT or SRT transcript, which becomes a meeting without audio.
• A clear-voice copy of a meeting's audio, if you make one: the audio with background noise removed on the phone. Nothing is sent anywhere.
• Photos you attach, the text read from them, and files you attach.
• Voice profiles you save: a voiceprint (numbers describing how a person sounds, used to recognise them in later meetings) and the short recordings it was made from. Ask people before saving their voice.
• Details from your calendar saved with a meeting: the event title, attendee names, and the name and time of an earlier event you link it to.
• Downloaded transcription and AI models, and the optional word re-timing model.
• Settings, including an AI endpoint address and API key if you enter them.
• Reports of the last three crashes or unexpected closes, with Android's record of a native crash where there was one.

BACKUPS
Recap opts out of Android's cloud backup and device-to-device transfer, so Android does not copy any of this off the phone. The in-app backup (Settings → Data) writes a file to a place you choose. It contains meetings, audio, photos, attached files and voice profiles, can be encrypted with a passphrase (AES-256), and never includes settings or API keys. Clear-voice copies are not included; they can be made again from the recording. Meetings in Recently deleted are not included either, nor are their files.

TRANSCRIPTION
By default Recap transcribes on the phone with a model you download once (Whisper, Parakeet or Nemotron). Until a model is downloaded, meetings are recorded as audio only and can be transcribed later. Neither the audio nor the words leave the phone. Speaker detection and voice profiles also work entirely on the phone. Imported recordings and videos are transcribed the same way; the sound of a video is taken out on the phone, and an imported WebVTT or SRT transcript is read on the phone. A transcription that stops part-way can be continued later from where it stopped, also on the phone. Clear voice, which removes background noise from a recording, uses a small model built into the app and runs on the phone too. After you edit a transcript, Re-time words can measure the timings of the edited words against the recording again (English only), with an optional model you download once; it runs on the phone, and nothing is sent.
If you turn off on-device transcription in Settings, Recap uses Android's speech service instead. On most phones that service is Google's, and Android documents that it is likely to send audio to remote servers; the speech provider's own privacy policy then applies. With "Prefer on-device transcription" on, phones running Android 12 or later that have an offline speech model use that instead. This engine keeps no recording.

READING TEXT IN PHOTOS
Text in photos you attach, such as a whiteboard, is read on the phone with Google's ML Kit text recognition, so you can search it and use it in summaries. The photos and their text are not sent anywhere for this. ML Kit does send Google diagnostic and usage-analytics information: details of the device, the app and the network connection (such as phone model, Android version, app version and connection type) and performance measurements, which may include identifiers used for those diagnostics. ML Kit starts with the app, so this can happen even if you never attach a photo. Google describes it in its ML Kit data disclosure.

AI SUMMARIES AND QUESTIONS
Summaries, answers, enhanced notes, titles and digests are made on the phone unless you set up an AI endpoint: by default with a built-in summariser, or with an AI model you download, which never uses the network.
If you turn on an AI endpoint, the meeting's transcript, notes, title, attendee names, text from its photos, your name (if you entered it) and the instructions of the summary style are sent to the address you entered, with your API key. That happens whenever you use an AI feature, or after every meeting if you turn on automatic summaries or titles and agree to send them. Asking across your library, a pre-meeting brief or a weekly digest sends excerpts from several meetings.
Local-only AI is on by default: Recap then sends only to this phone or your private network (for example Ollama on your computer), and plain http is never used outside your private network. If you turn Local-only AI off and use a cloud provider such as Groq or OpenRouter, that provider receives the data and its own terms and privacy policy apply.

MODEL DOWNLOADS
Models are downloaded only when you ask, over https, from Hugging Face (huggingface.co and its download servers) or GitHub (github.com and its download servers). Like any website, they see your IP address, which file is requested and the technical details Android sends with a web request, such as the Android version and phone model. Their own privacy policies apply. Nothing about your meetings is sent. The optional word re-timing model comes from the sherpa-onnx project's releases on GitHub, like some of the other models.

CRASH AND BUG REPORTS
If Recap crashes, or Android closes it because it stopped responding, ran short of memory or used too many resources, a report is saved on the phone: the app version, Android version, phone model and the technical error, which can include fragments of what the app was working on. When Android recorded the close (Android 11 and later), the report also notes which kind of on-device work and which model were running, how much memory Recap was using and how much memory the phone has; for a native crash (Android 12 and later), Android's full crash record is kept with it on the phone, and only a summary of the error and where it happened goes into the report. Recap never sends it. On the next launch you can share it through your own share sheet, to whoever you choose, or decline. Separately, if your phone shares usage and diagnostics with Google, Android may report crashes and freezes of any app, Recap included, to Google Play, which shows the developer aggregated statistics. That is a setting of your phone, not of Recap.
Report AI output, offered with summaries, answers and other generated text, opens a draft email to the developer in your own email app. It holds the reason you pick, your comment, where the text was shown, the app and Android versions, and the model and summary style used; the generated text itself is added only if you tick the box. Nothing is sent unless you send that email. If no email app can open it, the report is copied to the clipboard instead, and Recap keeps no copy of it.

SHARING AND EXPORT
When you share or export a meeting, audio, a clip, action items, a digest or a backup, it goes where you choose and is then outside Recap's control. Recap never shares your content on its own.
Exports of every kind (Markdown, PDF, Word, subtitles, and your whole library as Markdown files in a folder) are written only to a file or folder you pick in Android's picker, and Recap sends them nowhere. If you pick a location backed by a cloud service, that provider's own terms apply. For a library export, Recap keeps access to the folder you picked only while the export runs; if Android stops Recap during an export, Recap gives the access back the next time it starts.

NO ANALYTICS, ADS OR ACCOUNTS
Recap has no sign-in, shows no ads, and contains no analytics or tracking of its own. The developer does not receive or sell your data, and nothing is shared beyond the ML Kit diagnostics described above; the developer sees only reports or messages you choose to send.

PERMISSIONS
• Microphone: to record meetings (with a notification showing while a recording runs) and voice profiles (a 15-second capture on screen in Settings), only when you start one.
• Screen capture: only if you choose to record audio from other apps, such as a webinar. Android asks each time, and only the audio is captured, never the screen.
• Calendar (optional): read-only, as described below.
• Notifications: recording, transcription, clear-voice, passage removal, word re-timing and download progress, playback controls, reminders, meeting nudges, and storage clean-up notices if you turn automatic clean-up on. On Android 16 a recording, and work you start such as an import, can show as a Live Update in the status bar and at the top of the lock screen; you can turn Live Updates off for Recap in Android's Settings. When your lock screen hides notification contents, recording and transcription notifications show no meeting or file names there. The playback controls (on the lock screen, in the notification shade, and on connected headsets, cars and watches) show "Meeting audio" and "Recap", never the meeting's title.
• Internet: model downloads, your AI endpoint if you set one up, and ML Kit diagnostics.
• Network state: Recap uses it only to warn before a large model download over mobile data, and keeps and sends nothing about the network. Google's ML Kit also uses it, and its diagnostics include the type of connection (see READING TEXT IN PHOTOS).
• Running in the background, starting after a restart, exact alarms and keeping the phone awake: so recordings, transcriptions, clear-voice copies, passage removals, word re-timing and downloads finish with the screen off, a meeting you play keeps playing when you leave the app or lock the phone, reminders arrive on time, and a once-a-day job erases meetings whose 30 days in Recently deleted are up and runs automatic clean-up if you turn it on.
Photos come from your camera app or the system picker; Recap has no camera or photo-library permission. Files you import come from the share sheet, "Open with" or the system picker, which give Recap access to those files only; Recap has no storage permission.

CALENDAR
If you allow calendar access, Recap reads event titles, times and attendees on the phone to name meetings, suggest recording when one starts, and link follow-on meetings. Attendee email addresses are only used to make up a name when an attendee has none, and are not saved. Recap never changes your calendar and never sends calendar data anywhere, except as part of a meeting you send to an AI endpoint.

DELETING YOUR DATA
Deleting a meeting moves it, with its transcript, audio, clear-voice copy, photos and attached files, to Recently deleted (Settings → Data), where you can restore it for 30 days. Until then it stays on this phone, left out of your library, search, exports and backups, and nothing is sent anywhere. After 30 days, or at once if you choose Delete permanently or Empty there, the meeting and all its files are erased from the phone. The 30 days are counted by the phone's clock and never start before the latest date Recap has seen on it, so if the clock was once set ahead, a meeting deleted after it was put right is kept until 30 days after that date. You can also remove only a meeting's audio and keep its transcript, from the meeting's menu or from Settings → Data → Storage and clean-up. That Storage screen also deletes downloaded models you no longer use, and can turn on automatic clean-up: once a day, on the phone, it removes the audio of meetings, or moves the meetings themselves to Recently deleted, once they are older than a number of days you choose. Automatic clean-up is off unless you turn it on, and leaves starred and recently changed meetings alone. Erasing a meeting or removing its audio also deletes its clear-voice copy, and the copy can be deleted on its own from the player. Remove passage, in a transcript line's menu, deletes the words of the stretch you choose and, on the phone, replaces the recording with a copy in which that stretch is silent; the earlier recording, clips cut from it and its clear-voice copy are deleted. Summaries, the title, notes, action items, answers and chapter titles made before are not rewritten, so they may still mention that stretch until you generate them again, edit or delete them. Saved voices are deleted under Settings → Voice profiles, and downloaded models also from their lists in Settings. To remove everything, uninstall the app: Android's Manage space button for Recap opens Recap's Storage screen rather than clearing all of its data. Copies you exported or shared, and anything sent to a speech service or AI endpoint, are outside Recap and have to be deleted there.

SECURITY
You can require your fingerprint, face or screen lock to open Recap, and hide meeting content from screenshots and the recent-apps view. Every AI endpoint is checked against your Local-only AI setting before anything is sent, and model files are only accepted over https.

CHILDREN
Recap is not directed at children under 13. Apart from the ML Kit diagnostics described under READING TEXT IN PHOTOS, which include per-installation identifiers and go to Google, Recap collects no personal information from anyone: what you create stays on the phone unless you send it somewhere.

RECORDING OTHER PEOPLE
Recording people can require their consent depending on where you are. You are responsible for recording lawfully.

CHANGES
If this policy changes, the new version comes with an app update and is published at the same web address with a new effective date.

A private meeting recorder that transcribes, takes notes, and summarizes — on your device.

• Record, even in the background, and get the transcript on your phone after the meeting (live words optional in Settings)
• Tag speakers, highlight key moments, snap the whiteboard
• Summaries and "ask this meeting" via a local or your own LLM
• Offline transcription on the phone with Whisper, Parakeet or Nemotron
• Your meetings stay on your phone unless you choose to send them

Recap transcribes on this phone by default. Download a transcription model once in Settings; until then, meetings are kept as audio to transcribe later. Your meetings leave the phone only if you share them, switch to Android\'s speech service, or connect an AI endpoint. Reading text in photos uses Google\'s ML Kit, which sends Google diagnostic data, never the photos. Details are in the privacy policy in Settings.

Recording people can require their consent depending on your location and local laws. Make sure everyone is aware they\'re being recorded.
